candidates.prompt: A western gray squirrel (Sciurus griseus), single adult standing on all fours, side-on neutral pose, legs straight under the body, head level, tail held straight out behind and slightly raised, fully fluffed. Realistic proportions: 55 cm long, half of it tail; slim body; large rounded ears with no ear tufts. Silver gunmetal-grey back and flanks, pure white belly and chin with a sharp flank line, no brown or orange anywhere. Very long broad flat bushy tail, grey with a black inner band and a white fringe. Dark eye with a thin pale eye ring. No base, no ground. Game-ready, symmetric.

candidates.review: Reads as a tree squirrel at once: on all fours, slim straight forelegs, long flat hind feet, large rounded ears with no tufts (the red-squirrel fault the brief warned of is absent), symmetric. Faults: the tail is not straight out but curled in an S up over the back and down behind, and it is a round sausage (about 1.3 times as wide as deep, against a broad flat plume about 2.5 times) with no fringe; the hindquarters are heavy and pear-shaped; the eyes are modelled as closed lids; whiskers are modelled as thin strands. Tail length is about right (roughly half the total along its curve). Topology: 20,850 triangles, 17 pieces (the body plus whisker strands and small bits), 13 open edges, 1.0% slivers; 1.9 units long, +y up, nose toward +z. Build script: drop the whisker pieces, straighten the tail along a spline (or keep the curl as the pose and derive the straight rest), flatten and widen it in plan with a lighter fringe ring of faces, slim the haunches slightly, place a dark eye with a pale ring, recolour by region (silver grey, white belly, no brown).

accuracy_notes: Nothing adopted. A western gray is told from the introduced eastern gray and fox squirrels by a clean silver back and pure white belly with no brown or orange anywhere, and a very long broad flat plume with a black band inside a white fringe. The first Meshy candidate has the right body and ears but a round, curled tail; colour comes from the palette, not a texture.
